title: AuditStream: session-aware sampling and signature-based redaction for streamed responses
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: Current streaming telemetry emits verbatim streamed chunks into logs and traces which increases PII exposure risk and makes compliance for Private customers challenging. We also lack deterministic linkage between a streamed frame and its downstream tool/function calls for audits.

Goal: Build 'AuditStream' — a lightweight per-frame auditing layer that: (1) emits compact, privacy-preserving provenance for each streamed frame, (2) supports session-aware sampling and retention policies, (3) applies deterministic signature-based redaction that is reversible for authorized audits, and (4) works across hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and older client compat layers.

High-level approach:
- Envelope: extend the streaming envelope to include an optional audit header containing a short frame_signature and redaction_mask_version. The header is opaque to legacy clients (left in metadata) and processed by our observability pipeline.
- Signature: compute a HMAC-like signature over canonicalized frame content + session_id + model_version using a per-tenant audit key (KMS-managed). Store only truncated signature (e.g., 64 bits) in logs to allow sequence correlation without exposing content.
- Redaction: generate a deterministic redaction map for tokens/segments using the same canonicalization. The service writes a redaction_mask_version and counts (redacted_tokens) instead of raw text. Full plaintext reassembly is possible only through an authorized audit flow that requests reconstitution and is logged/approved.
- Sampling + retention: implement session-aware sampling policy that keeps all frames for error sessions (flagged by latency/trace errors) and samples non-error sessions at configurable rates. Private deployments may set sampling=0 by policy.
- Tracing integration: attach a lightweight frame_span to each frame that includes frame_signature and tool_call_markers. Ensure span propagation to tool/function callers so downstream services can correlate back to frame signatures.
- Compatibility: provide a server-side compat switch that falls back to prior envelope format for older SDKs; provide SDK changelog + migration guide.

Implementation notes:
- Add new telemetry metrics per frame: frame_latency_ms, frame_token_count, frame_kv_cache_hit (bool), frame_tool_calls (int), frame_redaction_hits (int), frame_signature_entropy (low|med|high).
- Storage/observability: stream audit headers to a separate high-throughput audit queue (Kafka topic: auditstream.v1) with encryption-at-rest and limited retention for hosted. Dedicated/Private will honor tenant retention policies.
- Keys: integrate with KMS for per-tenant audit keys. When a tenant rotates keys, signatures include key_id so old signatures remain verifiable by audit services if key is retained.
- Admin audit flow: build a gated server API for authorized reconstitution requests; every reconstitution request generates an immutable audit record and requires SSO approval.

Trade-offs considered:
- We avoid logging full frames to reduce PII surface but accept increased complexity for reconstitution workflows.
- Truncated signatures reduce collision resistance; chosen 64-bit truncation balances log-size vs correlation needs. We will monitor collision rate and increase if needed.
- Deterministic redaction may mask some non-PII context; acceptance criteria will include quality checks on structured output to ensure utility retained.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field for testable items.
acceptance_criteria: Audit header is attached to every streamed frame in canary and contains frame_signature and redaction_mask_version.
Observability pipeline receives per-frame metrics: frame_latency_ms, frame_token_count, frame_tool_calls, frame_redaction_hits and they appear on the AuditStream dashboard.
Tracing shows a frame_span that correlates streamed frames to downstream tool/function calls across service boundaries in 95% of sampled sessions.
Deterministic redaction removes PII from logs for sampled frames (verified by privacy unit tests) while allowing authorized reconstitution via the gated audit API.
Canary rollout (5% traffic) runs for 2 weeks without privacy or reliability incidents; rollback plan validated.
Compatibility mode works for legacy SDKs and is covered in migration doc: CONFLUENCE link present.
risks: Signature collision leading to incorrect correlation under high-volume customers.
Operational overhead for key management and reconstitution approvals.
Potential reduction in usefulness of streamed structured outputs if redaction overzealous.
Latency impact from computing signatures on high-throughput pads if not C-optimized.
